name: Mike Gushansky
bio1: It started with a borrowed turntable in a cramped apartment in [City], sometime around [Year]. A friend left it behind after a party, and I never gave it back. Within weeks I was spending every free hour digging through crates at flea markets, learning how one track could bleed into another and create something entirely new. Music became the thing that made everything else make sense.
bio2: Behind the decks, I gravitate toward the space where deep house meets something more textured and organic. I like long, slow builds and unexpected moments of silence. I've played rooftops in [City], warehouse parties in [City], and sunset sets on beaches where the bass feels like it's coming from the water itself. I'm drawn to sounds that move people without shouting at them — [Genre], [Genre], and everything in between.
bio3: Photography came later, but honestly it scratches the same itch. I shoot mostly on a [Camera] — street scenes, late-night moments, the kind of light that only lasts for a few minutes. I'm not interested in perfection. I want the photo to feel like a memory you're not sure is yours. Grain, shadow, and the occasional happy accident are my best friends in the edit.
bio4: Right now I'm splitting time between [City] and wherever the next gig or project takes me. I'm working on a new mix series, shooting a long-term photo project about nightlife culture, and always looking for the next collaboration that doesn't make sense on paper but feels right in the gut.
